first.rationale: Promotional pricing directly addresses competitive losses among price-sensitive SMBs and has prior acquisition and revenue evidence, but its sustainability and effect on qualified downstream revenue are not stated. Onboarding simplification matches the completion decline and may improve adoption, so verifying both records best informs the highest-consequence tradeoff before committing.

mid.rationale: Run a controlled onboarding-simplification experiment. The verified source directly addresses the current completion decline and showed completion +13%, time-to-value improved by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%, aligning better with sustainable qualified revenue. Reject promotional pricing because its +18% qualified-revenue lift was accompanied by 30-day retention falling 12% and failure at first renewal.

final2.rationale: Continue with onboarding simplification. Verified evidence shows completion +13%, time-to-value improved by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%, directly supporting sustainable revenue amid the current onboarding decline. The competitor's deeper cut increases urgency but does not reverse the verified downside of promotional pricing: 30-day retention fell 12% and the cohort failed to survive first renewal. This choice does not fully resolve immediate price-driven churn, but discounting would optimize short-term acquisition at the expense of the primary long-term objective.
